data.narrative:
Keen Technologies is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by John Carmack that has raised $20M to date. The broader Robotics & Manufacturing sector comprises 1 public comparable (ticker 277810.KQ) and 8 private peers including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI, though the company operates in a narrow segment with limited direct comparables at identical stage and valuation tier.

Given data constraints, only the Stage-Progression method is applicable here. This approach uses the $20M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement, implying a valuation of $50M. A Peer-Median approach could not be reliably applied due to insufficient narrow-set peers (fewer than 3 datapoints meeting same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier filters); broadening to the full sector of 11 peers would introduce material noise.

The triangulated analysis, constrained to a single methodology, supports a valuation range of $42M–$57M with a median of $50M. Key uncertainties center on (1) the applicability of 2.5x stage progression to this founder and sector versus empirical multiples in the current market; (2) lack of same-stage peer density to validate through market comparables; and (3) the absence of revenue or traction metrics to calibrate early-stage risk. Further fundraising signals or operational milestones would materially refine this range.
